articleTitle: On the precursory signature of Kobe earthquake on VLF subionospheric signals
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The subionospheric VLF Omega signal transmitted from Tsushima, Japan (geographic coordinates: 34/spl deg/37'N, 129/spl deg/27'E) is continuously received at Inubo (35/spl deg/42'N, 140/spl deg/52'E), and the propagation characteristics (especially phase) of this signal have exhibited abnormal behaviour (especially around the sunrise and sunset local times) a few days before the main shock of the 1995 Kobe earthquake. A statistical study based on long-term (four months before and four months after the earthquake) observational data has strongly suggested that this anomaly was not coincidental, but it is highly likely to be related to the earthquake. We have found from a computer simulation of VLF signal propagation that this observed effect can be explained by a decrease of about 1.5 km in the VLF reflection height. Plausible mechanisms for this decrease are discussed.

articleTitle: Development of low-cost high-resolution APD measuring equipment
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Given that amplitude probability distribution (APD) is an effective means of estimating the effects of electromagnetic disturbance on digital communications, we are now testing low-cost equipment for measuring APD at high resolution. The equipment combines multiple M-sequence counters having relatively prime periods and makes use of residue number systems (RNS) so that most of the circuits can be formed on one IC chip and a low-cost configuration can be achieved. In addition, the size of the discrete logarithm table, which is essential to restoring the enumerated value from the bit pattern output of the M-sequence counters, need be only 10/sup -5/ the size of a single M-sequence counter. By therefore arranging units of this APD measuring equipment into a parallel configuration, the processing speed can be increased by n times.

articleTitle: The dependence of the immunity of digital equipment on the hardware and software structure
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of immunity investigations on microcontrollers against impulsive disturbances described in this paper show that the susceptibility depends directly on the microcontroller's operational functions, especially on the microinstructions used for an assembler instruction. As a result, the fault frequency can change within some nanoseconds between 0% and 100%.

articleTitle: Receiver design of CDMA system for impulsive radio noise environment
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of a DS/CDMA system under an impulsive radio noise environment. First, by using the Middleton's (1977) class-A impulsive noise model, we evaluate the performance of conventional DS/CDMA system under impulsive radio noise and it is shown that the performance of the conventional DS/CDMA system is degraded by the effect of impulsive noise. Next, using the dependence between the quadrature components of impulsive radio noise, we propose a receiver designed for impulsive noise and evaluate the performance improvement achieved by this receiver. Moreover, in order to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed receiver for actual impulsive radio noise, we evaluate the performance of the receiver under microwave oven interference. Numerical results conclude that the performance of the DS/CDMA system is much improved by using the proposed receiver.

articleTitle: Effect of ferrite core attachment to coaxial cable on differential mode noise caused by braided shield current
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper examines whether the ferrite core attachment to a coaxial cable can be effective in suppressing the differential mode noise induced by a braided shield current. This noise is analyzed by using our equivalent circuit previously derived for the load effect produced by the ferrite core attachment.

articleTitle: Design and construction of stripline for measuring electromagnetic immunity of vehicular electrical cables
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A stripline for radiated susceptibility testing of vehicular components is designed and constructed. The stripline has the field uniformity of /spl plusmn/3 dB in the frequency range from 100 kHz to 500 MHz, and its characteristic impedance is 90 /spl Omega/. It has a high power capability by reason of using a tapered coaxial line instead of the traditional lumped circuit elements as the impedance matching unit.

articleTitle: Transient simulation of lossy multiconductor interconnects
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The transient simulation of electrically-long low-loss multiconductor interconnects is considered from a practical point of view. The importance of frequency dependent losses in these interconnects is discussed and a simple transmission line characterization procedure allowing for such losses is proposed. The characterization obtained yields simple and efficient interconnect models, that the user can include, without programming, in any simulator accepting differential operators.

articleTitle: Nature of the geoelectric field associated with GIC in long conductors such as power systems, pipelines, and phone cables
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electric fields can be resolved into scalar potential and vector potential terms that are respectively irrotational and solenoidal: E=-/spl nabla//spl phi/-/spl part/A/sup s///spl part/t. It is shown that these parts can be uniquely identified with different sources: a distribution of charge and a changing magnetic field. Examining induction in a uniform and non-uniform earth shows that the geoelectric field affecting long conductors is principally due to an induced electric field associated with magnetic field changes. Potential gradients are a secondary effect that results from charge accumulation at conductivity boundaries. The electric field experienced by a long conductor at the Earth's surface extending from point a to point b can be represented by a voltage source V/sub ab/=/spl int//sub a//sup b/E.dl where, because of the vector potential part of the electric field integration has to be done along the path of the conductor.

articleTitle: Computation and measurement of electrical interference effects in aqueducts due to a nearby parallel transmission line
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A study has been conducted to determine the electromagnetic interference effects in aqueducts which are parallel to a nearby transmission line. A mitigation system has been designed to reduce these interference levels. Field measurements have been carried out to verify the computed electromagnetic interference levels in the aqueducts during steady-state and fault conditions with mitigation installed. The results show that the measured interference levels are in good agreement with the computed data.

articleTitle: Validation of field-to-transmission line coupling models
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents experimental validations of field-to-transmission line coupling models using EMP simulators. Several configurations have been considered such as single-wire lines, multiconductor lines, and ramified lines above a conducting ground plane. All these structures were terminated in different ways (open circuit, short circuit, matched). Comparisons between calculations using transmission line theory and experimental measurements are presented and discussed. In general, agreement between numerical calculations and measurements is found to be reasonably good and validate the coupling models widely used today by the EMC community.

articleTitle: IEC standardization of Immunity to High Altitude Nuclear Electromagnetic Pulse (HEMP)
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The IEC, the International Electrotechnical Commission, the authority for world standards in electrical and electronics engineering, is elaborating standardization of "Immunity to High Altitude Nuclear Electromagnetic Pulse (HEMP)". This paper gives information concerning the IEC, the organization of the HEMP standard, the progress of work, and some highlights of the present results.

articleTitle: Lightning radiation field due to channel tortuosity and branching
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The effect of lightning channel branching on the temporal waveform of the radiated fields of the return stroke is modeled. The effect of branching is isolated, and compared to the effect of tortuosity of an unbranched channel.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic leakage and protection for computer
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper researches a computer's electromagnetic leakage and information leakage path, protection measures, computer CRT ray and synchronous signal radiation field amplitude, and leakage information restoration. It presents two new computer leakage measure techniques.

articleTitle: VHF sporadic E-a significant factor for EMI
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Sporadic E, or Es, is an ionospheric propagation mode which is useless for service but is crucial in estimating interference at VHF. It is particularly important in Asia where temperate latitude sporadic E has its summer and yearly peak. Examples are given of the reduction in broadcast service area and year-to-year variability at the 99% of the time service level.

articleTitle: TEM horn antenna for the time domain shielding effectiveness measurement
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The design and construction of a TEM horn antenna to be used for the time domain measurement of the shielding effectiveness of materials is described and measurement results of its characteristics in time domain and frequency domain using the two-antenna method are compared. The constructed TEM horn has the bandwidth of above 2 GHz.

articleTitle: Performance of radio communication systems under microwave oven interference environment
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The effect of microwave oven interference on the performance of several digital radio communications systems (PDC, PHS, ISM-band wireless LAN) is investigated. First, we measure the interference emitted from microwave ovens and it is shown that a high level interference is emitted from microwave ovens and its emission interval is matched with the powerline cycle. By using the measurement results, the performance of /spl pi//4-shift QDPSK and DS/CDMA systems are evaluated. Numerical results show that the performance of /spl pi//4-shift QDPSK is degraded by the effect of microwave oven interference. Moreover, it is shown that, for the case of the TDMA multiple access scheme, since the high level interference is emitted periodically, the specified channel suffers from the high level interference.

articleTitle: Development of coupling and decoupling networks below 150 kHz
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Four types of coupling and decoupling networks (CDNs) were developed to measure the immunity of telecommunications equipment below 150 kHz on a power line terminal and a telecommunications line terminal. The developed CDNs satisfy the specifications for the design objective. An experiment using the developed CDNs indicates that the malfunction of the actual disturbance can be estimated from the immunity test results.

articleTitle: Estimation of internal impedances of digital ICs
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a method of estimating the internal impedance and the internal source voltage of digital ICs at electromagnetic interference frequencies. Estimates of the internal impedance of various types of CMOS digital ICs in operation-clock frequencies are performed. The result shows that there is a difference between the values of the internal impedance in the operation-clock frequencies and the values of the internal impedance measured by direct current. It is concluded that the output current from digital ICs when the load is changed can be estimated in accordance with the obtained values of the internal impedance of the digital ICs in the operation-clock frequencies.

articleTitle: Calculation of conductive effects on earth return circuits
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents an analytical-numerical solution for the potentials and currents excited along buried conductors (earth return circuits) by the conductive effects of the quasistationary electric flow field produced in the earth by earthing arrangements. It is assumed that the system considered is linear and that the earth is an isotropic, homogeneous medium of finite conductivity. The reaction of currents floating in the underground conductor on the currents in the earthing devices is disregarded. The transmission line model of the earth return circuit, a segmental approximation of the curve of the primary potential distribution along the conductor and the concept of superposition have been used in the method. The method may be useful for an evaluation of the conductive effects on the earth return circuits in many practical cases, which are connected with power supply systems, electric traction and cathodic protection as well. The technical application of the method presented is illustrated by an example.

articleTitle: Recent developments in elastomeric EMI shielding gasket design
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Some recent developments in electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials are discussed. Finite element analysis (FEA) concepts and techniques for assisting EMI shielding gasket design are introduced. A design optimization of a composite plastic/elastomer gasket for EMI shielding of an advanced cellular telephone handset application is presented.

articleTitle: Characterization of electromagnetic shield
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Most often electromagnetic (EM) shielding components (e.g. gaskets, ventilation panels, housings, etc.) are designed and characterized individually. There are many documented techniques on how to characterize the EM shielding components. However, when all of the shielding components are assembled into an enclosure, the overall EM shielding shows significantly different and usually worse results. This paper introduces a technique which will effectively characterize the EM shielding of the complete assembly in a way simulating its actual use. This technique, when applied with a battery driven signal source, can also eliminate the error due to the presence of power or signal cable acting as an antenna in the test setup.

articleTitle: Metallization of plastics for shielding
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For a satisfactory performance in accordance with EMC, every electrical and electronic equipment requires a housing, which offers adequate protection related to radiated emissions, as well as immunity against electromagnetic fields acting from outside. For this purpose plastic housings were metallized with a variety of metals by various technologies. These housings have been evaluated in view of their shielding efficiency and environmental considerations of the production process.

articleTitle: EMC considerations in spacecraft harness design
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A spacecraft harness or electrical distribution system (EDS) provides a functional interface between various subsystems of the spacecraft and is a major path for interference coupling. Hence, an electromagnetic interference (EMI) distribution system may be inadvertently built into the EDS, causing inconsequential to catastrophic failures. It is therefore essential to meet the EMC requirements while designing the EDS. This paper outlines EMI coupling reduction techniques, grounding and bonding schemes adopted, proper routing, harness fabrication materials, steps involved in making a typical spacecraft harness and validation of the designed EDS using in-house software.

articleTitle: Models of a cable bunch formed by twisted three-phase cables
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We investigate the magnetic field of a bunch of twisted three-phase cables of finite length which are statistically ordered with respect to their installation angles. After deriving integral expressions for the magnetic induction of a single three-phase cable a specific model is proposed which requires no integration. As results of statistical investigations we show that the field of a cable bunch consisting of a sufficient number of cables can be expressed with adequate accuracy by the reduced field of a single cable which leads the overall current of the bunch.

articleTitle: Does an overhead lightning protection system protect structures against nearby strikes?
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The presence of an overhead lightning protection system designed to protect structures from direct lightning attachments will alter the electromagnetic (EM) environment surrounding the structures located at the space launch pads. This analysis addresses the overhead protection system's effectiveness against the EM environment generated by the protection system in the case of more frequently occurring nearby strikes.

articleTitle: Determining radiation characteristics of a practical source with a TEM cell
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The results of electromagnetic fields radiated from an unknown electrically small source, obtained by measurement inside a TEM cell and above an open area test site, are analyzed to confirm their equivalence. Our purposes are to find an algorithm and to establish a standard method for EMI measurement by using a TEM cell for frequencies below several hundreds megahertz.

articleTitle: Calibration method and device of surface current probe
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the calibrating method and device of surface current probe used in EMC measurement. In this kind of method a parallel-plate transmission line is used to establish known, uniform surface current and determine the transfer impedance of the surface current probe. This paper provides the experimental data and graphs, and analyzes uncertainty of measurement.

articleTitle: Measurement uncertainty in EMI emission measurements
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes the present trend in international standardization regarding the EMC measurement uncertainty. It gives a basis for the calculation of an uncertainty budget with an example and some practical guidelines for the reduction of emission measurement uncertainty.

articleTitle: The application of the CPD method in the analysis of the EM field excited by vertical electric dipoles over horizontally stratified media
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new analytic method for the electromagnetic field in stratified media-the counter-propagation deduction (CPD) method has been suggested by the authors, which, by introducing a new concept-the boundary originated set (BOS) of waves, is characterized by constructing or deducing the solutions directly, and can provide direct mathematic expressions of the fields in an arbitrary layer convenient for numerical evaluation by computer programming. This paper discusses its application in the analysis of the electromagnetic field excited by vertical electrical dipoles.

articleTitle: A study of automobile electromagnetic disturbance or noise source
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper studies the most serious electromagnetic radiation noise source during the engine ignition system operation, and some main noise frequency ranges are given. The aim is to help the reduction of the ignition noise.

articleTitle: EMI shielding-common problems and containment strategies
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This discussion focuses on the sources and containment strategies for EMI. The operation of all electrical and electronic devices involves the changing of voltage or current levels either intermittently or continuously, sometimes at very fast rates. This results in the development of electro-magnetic energy at discrete frequencies as well as over frequency bands. The circuit will radiate this energy into the surrounding area and also into the wiring emerging along the external power, signal and control lines. It is this electro-magnetic energy which must be contained to meet international standards such as FCC (U.S.) or EC Directive (Europe). A gasket is required when the gaps, slots and holes around the connector/metal plate interface are such that they allow excessive radiation of the internally generated electro-magnetic frequencies, and if such radiation causes the equipment to emit electro-magnetic interference or is susceptible to such interference outside of the permitted levels.

articleTitle: IC models for the simulation of the emission radiated from PCB
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The authors are developing the technology that can simulate normal-mode emission radiated from printed circuit boards. We describe the driver and the receiver IC models which are needed to simulate radiated emission. We have derived the driver and the receiver IC models. The validity of these models was confirmed by comparing measured data with the results of the simulation.

articleTitle: Installation of EMI mitigation for information technology environments
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Information technology (I/T) has evolved to being a critical element of our world wide business and personal lives. While designed to meet electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) standards, the high speed functions of a computing system are exposed to external sources of electromagnetic interference (EMI). Support environments should be designed to mitigate EMI, thus complementing designed system availability.

articleTitle: Low frequency screening effect in urban areas and the engineering measurement technology
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The low frequency screening effect is very good in urban districts because of a lot of underground metallic pipes. There are not only remarkable technology-economic benefits but also society benefits when considering this screening effect, which is named the city environment screening factor in practical engineering constructions. The theory of the low frequency screening effect of a multiconductor system is discussed in the paper. Then the engineering measurement technology and instruments of the screening effect are introduced in detail. Some successful application samples of the technology are presented. In general, the value of the city environment screening factor often can be 0.5 to 0.8, the lowest value may be 0.1, the highest may be 0.8 to 0.9.

articleTitle: Adaptive filter using decision-feedback to suppress BPSK interference in spread spectrum systems
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The research results on tone interference suppression are extended to BPSK interference suppression by analyzing the signal characteristics of the BPSK interference. Methods including one called "sign inversion of interference estimation output controlled by error" are promoted and the valid conditions of the method are analyzed. Simulation results show that applying the new method under valid conditions can make more significant improvement (about 26 dB) in the convergence performance of algorithms for suppressing BPSK type narrow band interference than previous results made without the new method.

articleTitle: The TEM cell test method (for road vehicle electronic components)
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The automotive industries developed test methods in the field of the "electromagnetic compatibility" (EMC). This paper describes the TEM cell component test method, which in comparison of other component test methods can easily be used for susceptibility- and emission tests. The paper describes the test set-up, susceptibility test, and the emission test and gives some hints on the correlation to whole vehicle tests.

articleTitle: Development of standard monopole antenna for antenna factor measurement
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a brief design result and calibration procedure for a vertically polarized monopole antenna in the 30 kHz-300 MHz frequency range at the Korea Research Institute of Standards and Science (KRISS). The standard field method is used to calculate the vertical electric field. The calculated and measured antenna factors are also presented.

articleTitle: Spectrum management and electromagnetic compatibility for today's communication
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper illustrates the importance of spectrum management which is closely related to the emerging technology. As devices of an electronic and electromagnetic nature grow in complexity, the capability of EMC is already of profound importance and will increase as we rely more and more upon technology. The article introduces some new work carried out in China, points out that CDMA will be the advanced technology in the area of effective usage of frequency spectrum resource and EMC issues, and describes the compatibility analysis between FPLMTS and space systems. It also discusses the definitions and conventions, applications of EMC in systems operations, and the policy review of the use and management of the radio spectrum.

articleTitle: Numerical dispersive characteristics and stability condition of the multi-resolution time-domain (MRTD) method
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The numerical dispersive characteristics and the stability condition of the multi-resolution time-domain (MRTD) method are calculated. A dispersion analysis of the MRTD schemes including a comparison to Yee's (1966) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is given. The superiority of the MRTD method to the spatial discretization is shown. The results show that the required computational memory can be reduced by using the MRTD method. The MRTD method is a very useful method for the numerical modelling of electromagnetics.

articleTitle: On the equivalence between radiation and injection in BCI testing
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Bulk current injection (BCI) and field coupling are analytically compared in order to ascertain if current injection tests are adequate for susceptibility assessment of electronic equipment. Transmission line theory is adopted for modelling wiring harnesses, and the equivalence is discussed by comparing the effects that the two kinds of excitation techniques produce at the line ends. General results are obtained, which are not affected by any assumptions on the equipment under test. It is shown that, from the theoretical point of view, injection by means of two current probes allows equivalence with any radiated plane wave excitation. The equivalence is achieved by controlling the clamp voltage in order to match the incident field characteristics.

articleTitle: Threshold of perception for capacitor discharge on the human body
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The study reports on capacitor discharge on the human body. Experiments show that the capacitor value has great effect on the threshold voltage: when the value is small the threshold voltages of people are very different from each other; this difference becomes smaller and smaller when the capacitor value increases. This paper also reports on the charge and the power of discharge. An experimental formula about the charge and the capacitor is also presented.

articleTitle: Measurement of voltage rise curves due to gap discharge using coupled transmission lines in distributed constant line system
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Very fast voltage rise curves due to gap discharge were examined to discuss an EMI source. The measurement system consists of a distributed constant line system, because the voltage transients were very rapid. A characteristic of the gap electrode, which has a matched impedance for the distributed constant line system, was investigated in the frequency range below 5 GHz. The voltages of the power source in the experiment were 510 V and 800 V because Paschen's law holds its stability in the air condition. It was confirmed that the measurement method enables one to measure high speed voltage rise curves of about 100 ps.

articleTitle: Time- and frequency-domain coupling analysis of field-to-nonuniform transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The coupling of an external electromagnetic wave to a nonuniform transmission line (TL) of finite-length suspended above a conducting ground plane is considered. The externally excited nonuniform TL is approximated by a cascaded series of uniform TLs together with a suitable set of equivalent distributed voltage and current sources along the line to account for the effect of the external source. A few typical line geometries, relevant in the EMC field, are studied to confirm the validity of this method. Comparison of this approach with the rigorous MoM solution and laboratory experiments indicates that this simple circuit-theory-based method provides reliable results.

articleTitle: A fractal model for the lightning induced current on a transmission line
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This article presents a model of a tortuous lightning channel, and a study of the consequent electromagnetic coupling to a transmission line. We analyse the fractal dimension of the induced current on the line, compared with the fractal dimension of the lightning channel and the impinging electromagnetic field on the line. This comparison confirms our previous studies pointing out that the channel fractal dimension and the electromagnetic field fractal dimension are related (in particular, for typical lightning parameters they are the same). A comparison of simulated fields and line currents with experimental measurements is also attempted.

articleTitle: A new method to predict the crosstalk of multiconductor transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Crosstalk in multiconductor transmission lines is predicted by using a method of combining the method of moments with finite-difference time domain (FDTD) method. To evaluate the lossy skin-effect lines, quadrature formulae and recursive convolution are used to get accurate results. The modified MTL equations are solved by the FDTD method plus the terminal conditions. Harmonic basis functions and point matching are applied to obtain the capacitance and inductance matrices of transmission lines above a perfect ground plane.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic compatibility of antennas on a mobile board
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents solutions to the problem of optimizing the decrease of antenna coupling coefficients on a mobile board for the case of limitations on the coverage for each antenna. To determine the minimum value of the antenna coupling coefficient for one pair of antennas we use the Gauss-Zeidel optimization method or the search method. When two or several antenna pairs have a common antenna the coordinates of this antenna are determined by compromise. The algorithms of optimum antenna placement are supported by computer software and are tested for the case of four antennas.

articleTitle: Studies on characteristics of absorbing materials
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Presently the electromagnetic characteristics of absorbing materials have been partly studied on basis of Maxwell equations. However, a thorough study for a physics view-point is obviously insufficient. A new concept, power flux turning, is proposed. We analyzed the absorbing materials' characteristics by the method of the power flux, and found that power flux turning relates strongly with the absorbing materials' characteristics. Power flux turning keeps the absorbing materials' characteristics against improving.

articleTitle: The effect of segmented metal plane in microstrip structure
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: When the ground plane of a multi-layered PCB (microstrip structure) is partly segmented under a signal strip, the radiated emission of the structure significantly increases. We model several cases which can be typical structures in PCBs and calculate those cases of the segmented structures with a method of moments based electromagnetic simulator. The experiments were followed with generic type antennas and a semi-anechoic chamber; the results are very useful for EMC designers to make actual PCB designs.

articleTitle: A automatic measurement system of mobile communication field strength
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper puts forward an automatic measurement system for mobile communication field strength analysis. It introduces the measurement system software and the technology. The system changes the sample frequency according the speed of the measurement vehicle to ensure the sample interval distance required by mobile communication field strength measurement theory. It analyses the statistics of the measurement data while the measurement is being carried out. The system can be used in various cases of land mobile field strength measurement.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic interference problems in mobile wireless communication system and its efficient frequency management
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper dwells on the design and development aspect of modern electronic wireless communication system taking into consideration of the EMC aspect, viz. propagation characteristics, multipath reflection, adjacent channel interference, co-channel interference, environmental norms, fading etc. It deals with the problems of echo-cancellation due to high speed modems and loss of signal due to power level change during operation. Besides, sectorisation for using the same line on the same cell-site by added users is also discussed.

articleTitle: Experimental evaluation of MSK and GMSK with differential detection in non-Gaussian impulsive noise environment
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: By employing a composite noise generator (CNG) to simulate non-Gaussian impulsive noise, the bit error rate (BER) for minimum shift keying (MSK) and Gaussian filtered minimum shift keying (GMSK) with differential detection are evaluated experimentally. An upper bound of BER for MSK is also given.

articleTitle: Simulations of time selective fading mobile radio channel
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To simulate the time-selective behavior of urban microcell mobile radio channels, a method is presented, which is based on a physical model for the radio wave propagation process in these environments. The approach enables a generation of complex impulse responses as given by the statistics of the underlying channel behavior. Fading characteristics of the multipath structures can be efficiently simulated by reproducing the physical wave interference process, thereby incorporating the different channel characteristics that are observed in different urban environments.

articleTitle: Electric field strength distribution around man model exposed to the radiation of cellular phones
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A numerical modeling of human body is established by dividing it into various layers for calculating the electric field strength distributions inside and outside the man model, which is exposed to cellular phone radiation at a frequency of 900 MHz and a power of 0.5 W. Calculations are made by using the finite difference time-domain (FDTD) method. A type of imaginary microwave absorber, which is attached to the edges of the problem geometry, is used to simulate the absorption boundary required by the application of the FDTD method. The results are useful for the further study of the effects on the human body of the radiation from cellular phones.

articleTitle: Gaussian and non-Gaussian statistics
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The article presents a description of Gaussian statistical theory in relation to signal analysis. Special attention is placed on the correlation phenomena and the spectra. The main part of the paper deals with the higher-order statistics. The notions of the 3rd-moment and the cumulant function are introduced and their relation to the spectra and the physical parameters of signals are explained on the basis of examples.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic environment of an automobile controlled by computer and raising reliability measure
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Automotive electromagnetic environments are analysed. In view of the reliability designs, for instance, in the entirety, hardware and software, etc., the paper focuses on a description of the reliability measures of automotive microcomputer control systems.

articleTitle: Cellular sectorial radio relay stations-radiation safety to personnel
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the results of a survey conducted by RAFAEL-'hazards of electromagnetic radiation to personnel (HERP)' in the vicinity of sectorial radio relay stations (SRRS) operated by cellular telephone carriers in Israel. The major conclusions of the HERP survey are: the power densities in the vicinity of the SRRS were found to be below the International Radiation Protection Association (IRPA) general public permissible exposure limits (PEL). Typical radiation levels were less than 10% of the IRPA PEL. At some of the sites the total power density as measured with a broadband radiation monitor exceeded 0.5-1 mW/cm/sup 2/ (PEL at 890 MHz=0.44 mW/cm/sup 2/). A narrowband measurement that was performed using antennas and a spectrum analyzer was necessary for extracting the exact radiation spectra of the SRRS which never exceeded 5%-10% of IRPA PEL.

articleTitle: Analysis of multiband electromagnetic shielding effectiveness
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The application of transmission-line modeling (TLM) in electromagnetic shielding effectiveness (SE), which developed the plane-wave shielding theory, was described to single-layered and multilayered media. For application of design, the basic expressions of SE were presented with general parameters, which being use to calculate SE of a multilayered media and even to calculate SE with multiband for vertical or oblique incidence to lossless isotropic medias including dielectric and metallic layers. Finally, the analysis and design of SE of a type A sandwich with multiband were presented.

articleTitle: Some experimental results for the head/hand effects in personal communications
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work, some experimental results for the head/hand effects in personal communications are presented, for the real situation of a person during a call in the AMPS system. The hand-held unit has a monopole antenna. A simple measurement procedure is described and experimental results are discussed including biological effect aspects and wireless communication system performance. The obtained results will instigate other researchers to carry out a better characterization of the head/hand-handset interaction in personal communication systems.

articleTitle: The improvement of non-selection characteristics on semiconductor digital multiplexer
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In a semiconductor digital multiplexer (using photo MOS relays) in order to select one of the many pulse-train signals with fast rise/fall time, leakage of the pulse train is observed at a non-selection point due to stray capacity existing on the non-selection switch. This paper proposes a leakage suppression circuit, and proves the effectiveness of it analytically and experimentally.

articleTitle: The research of protection from EMP of civil shelter
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The authors have been engaged in research of EMP protection engineering for several years and have completed a number of EMP protection designs for shelters. This paper gives some design requirements of EMP protection of dug up civil shelters and places emphasis on common protection steps, and their real measured shielding effectiveness and appraisement.

articleTitle: Magnetic field of transmission line above uniform Earth
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, based on Maxwell's equations, we obtained the calculation formulas of the magnetic field of a horizontal current above a uniform Earth, and give the calculation formulas of the magnetic field in air of an infinite horizontal current. Using them we give the magnetic field distribution of an actual example.

articleTitle: EMC-driven placement for MCM
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, we use the hierarchical placement algorithm to implement EMC driven MCM placement. To ensure that every maximal connection chip pairs are placed as close as possible, we provide a clustering development algorithm. A proper model for EMC-driven MCM placement is used in this work. By this model, we use a short wire antenna to simulate the radiation of each chip on the substrate. At present, we have implemented an MCM placement program successfully, and this program can output the layout with a CIF form.

articleTitle: Direction finding on far-distance lightnings
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Based on the data recorded in Wuchang, Zhanjiang and Guilin in China on January 5 1988, the four-parameter method (FPM) and the goniometer method (GM) are used in direction finding on far-distance lightning. The results met the case of the cloud chart on that day.

articleTitle: Reduction of stress voltages at control equipment terminals in a substation through inductive coupling between cable core and sheath
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Considerable potential differences can develop between different parts, of an electric station's grounding grid during fault conditions, when circulating currents of great magnitude are involved. As a result, communications or control wires extending between these locations can subject the equipment they serve to damaging stress voltages. A limited reduction of the stress voltages can be achieved by increasing the density of grounding grid conductors. This paper examines a highly effective method of reducing stress voltages by enclosing these wires in low impedance metallic sheaths or conduit, and bonding the latter outer conductors to the grounding grid at the wire extremities.

articleTitle: Absorbing materials optimization on characteristic parameters
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Many mathematical methods have been used in absorbing materials optimization on characteristic parameters, but none is efficient all the time. We believe that before optimization a thorough study of the object function should be done. We analyzed the characteristics of this object function, and drew some useful conclusions for the absorbing materials' parameter optimization. These conclusions are suitable for the optimization of thickness, and the complex permittivity and complex permeability. Using this conclusion, optimization will become much more simple and convenient.

articleTitle: Crosstalk between nonparallel transmission lines of finite length
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Crosstalk or coupling between two nonparallel transmission lines of finite length is studied by using a circuit concept. The phenomenon can be estimated by a similar way as the coupling of external electromagnetic fields to a transmission line. The external fields can be considered as distributed voltage and current sources expressed as vector potentials. From solutions of the transmission line equations, a four-port network expression can be derived. The crosstalk is analyzed by the four-port network in terms of the terminal voltages and currents. Experiments for some models were conducted; the measured results are in a good agreement with the theory.

articleTitle: Experimental verification of OATS field distribution predicted by mutual impedance coupling model
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Experimental results are reported for open area test site (OATS) field distribution as a function of measuring antenna height in the frequency range 30 MHz to 990 MHz for 3 m and 10 m ranges. Measured data are in agreement with predicted values derived from models based on mutual impedance coupling between antennas and ground plane image antennas. Variations due to site anomalies are also discussed.

articleTitle: The measurement study of radiated emission for chip microcomputer development system
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the principle and method of chip microcomputer radiated emission using a TEM cell. It gives the calculation formulas of equivalent radiated power in free space. It also gives the emission measurement result for the MCS-51 chip microcomputer development system in the frequency band 0.15 MHz-30 MHz and gives further explanations.

articleTitle: General strategy for designing a low-radiation computer
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper provides the necessary background and step-by-step procedures to design a computer that neither radiates undesired signals in excess of the applicable specifications nor interferes with itself or other equipment in its vicinity.

articleTitle: Research on near field of airborne short wave antenna
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The near field of a Boeing 707 320B aircraft excited by its short wave antenna has been calculated and analyzed using the FDTD method after modeling aircraft and short wave antenna by the B-spline method. This research can provide data for the further study of the short wave antenna's impedance character, far field pattern and mutual interference between short wave communication and other electronic equipment, it can play an important role in aircraft EMC analysis and design.

articleTitle: Simulation of the field characteristics of TEM cell using the TLM method
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The field distributions of a TEM cell with finite depth of the inner conductor are simulated by using the TLM method. Numerical results show that, both of the cut-off wavelength and field distributions vary with the size of the inner conductor. It also shows that the TLM method can be conveniently and effectively used to analyze and design the TEM cell for EMC measurement.

articleTitle: The use of detectors instead power meters: a simple and cheap option in microwave measurements
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this article, the use of microwave detectors (Schottky diodes) instead power meters is suggested. With this simple substitution, microwave measurements may become an easier and cheaper process. The detector specifications are described. In order to exemplify the proposed substitution, experimental results are presented and, when compared to numerical ones, a good agreement is observed. The detector's stability and price are some of the advantages of the suggested substitution.

articleTitle: Mathematical model of predicting power frequency electric field round the corner of high voltage transmission lines
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The mathematical model of predicting power frequency (PF) electric field round the corner of high voltage transmission lines and the calculating methods of potential and field strength were introduced in this paper. The deduced formulas were symmetrical which were convenient for the calculation. The results of calculation and measurement were identical in the main.

articleTitle: Development of a fractional loop antenna for EMC measurement
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A newly developed EMC (electromagnetic compatibility) antenna is proposed in this paper which can simulate highly directive standard EM (electromagnetic) waves. The proposed antenna can be made by placing a one-sixth of conducting loop-wire (H-loop) in front of a 60/spl deg/ degree corner reflector. The mathematical model of such a quasi-shield probe called an H-loop is developed. The characteristics of this antenna have been compared with those of the existing quarter loop antenna and a complete loop antenna. The input impedance of the developed antenna is computed from the network representation of the H-loop antenna.

articleTitle: A study of second reflection effects of high voltage transmission line on HF antenna radiation characteristic by scaling model
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper introduces a study of high voltage transmission line second reflection effects on short-wave radio communication in a semi-anechoic chamber using a scaling model. Comparison measurements show that transmitter antenna radiation angle and half power point angle is not seriously affected by high voltage transmission line.

articleTitle: Experience in the implementation of the basic automated spectrum management system (BASMS) of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU)
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper concerns the experience gained in the implementation in the Kyrgyz Republic of the first official ITU spectrum management software, the basic automated spectrum management system (BASMS). Some advice on the BASMS operation are presented. Particularly, an advanced classification system of administrative record codes (ADMIN ID-s) for the BASMS practical operation is proposed. Features of the BASMS option "interference calculation" and "frequency assignments" are also discussed and a detailed interpretation of the results of calculations is referred to.

articleTitle: A simple approach for estimating the radiation envelope of an entire short wave broadcast station
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Shortwave radio broadcast stations are often located in the vicinity of air traffic routes and even near airports. Aircraft flying in the vicinity of such broadcast stations may be exposed to extremely high radiated electromagnetic fields, which may interfere with on board electronic systems and radio receivers. This paper presents a simple approach, based on the use of electronic worksheets (e.g., "Lotus", "Excel", etc.) for estimating the "radiation envelopes" (i.e., the radiation pattern) of the station. A similar approach was applied for electromagnetic coupling computations. This approach requires only the antenna manufacturer's radiation patterns (in all slewing modes), and the operational modes of the transmitters.

articleTitle: Large scale computing system EMI test philosophy
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The purpose of the paper is to discuss the testing philosophy of large system EMI testing and some of the methods used to reduce the test logistics and complexity; it is also for Regulatory Agents to consider when writing up EMC rules. Actual test data are given to substantiate the rationales behind the test methods.

articleTitle: PULP, an educational software package for line parameters calculation
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents PULP, a MATLAB-based package for the determination of the per-unit-length parameters for lossless multiconductor transmission lines. The inductance and capacitance matrices are determined by the finite element method for an extended set of practical interest structures. These include cables with circular cross-section and multilayered structures. The package is loaded with an easy-to-use graphical user interface that makes it suitable for the interactive input of the geometry, simulation, and output of the parameters.

articleTitle: Directional antennas standardization
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the literature and internationally accepted standardization procedures the problem of directional antennas standardization in the frequency range below 1 GHz still has not been satisfactorily solved. The applicability of a typical standard receiving antenna method for this purpose is being considered. It is proven that the method can be applied directly or its accuracy could be increased by relative simple means. The idea is discussed using an example of a logo-periodic antenna, but the method may be applied to any other one and the conclusion is valid for other types of antennas. Apart from the correct standardization of a directional antenna antenna its applicability to EMF measurements especially in conditions of interfering fields and multipath propagation, may be dramatically limited as a result of the nonacceptable level of measuring error. The reasons for the limitations are briefly outlined.

articleTitle: A 12 GHz band linearly polarized high-gain microstrip array antenna study
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, the development of a linearly polarized microstrip array antenna with a gain of 34 dB at 12 GHz is presented. The antenna is applied for receiving direct broadcasts from a satellite. This antenna is parallel and series fed by microstrip transmission lines, and as a result it has high efficiency and low cross-polarization.

articleTitle: The new EEC directive on EMC in motor vehicles (95/54 EEC/Nov. 95) (for road vehicle and electric/electronic components)
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The growth in the use of electronic components in road vehicles has made it necessary to install a new directive for government testing, type approval and the release procedure in the field of EMC road vehicles for Europe. This paper describes the new regulation 94/54 EEC from Nov. 1995 in detail, that means the history with the old EEC 72/245, development, requirements, definitions e.g. broadband/narrowband, vehicle and component test methods including limits for emission and immunity.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of electromagnetic compatibility between GSM-900 cellular networks and REE of the aeronautical radionavigation service
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper deals with a EMC problems between the GSM-900 general-purpose land mobile network and the radio electronic equipment (REE) of the aeronautical radionavigation service resulting from the national special features of the frequency allocations in Russia. Presented are the results of bench testing aimed at determination of the signal-to-interference ratio at the ARNS aircraft receiver input in the presence of unintended interference from GSM-900 network REE. The paper also describes the results of the flight test for evaluation of the ranges of interfering effects.

articleTitle: Calculation of the electric and magnetic fields near energy objects
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Numerical techniques developed by the authors for industrial frequency (50 or 60 Hz) electromagnetic field calculation are discussed. The FIELD 3.0 program for electronetwork object (transmission lines and substations) field computation is presented. The calculation method takes buildings, transports and biological objects into account.

articleTitle: Antenna model for EMI evaluation
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper provides some approximate methods of antenna gain calculation which are often met under several conditions in EMI evaluation. It also tests and verifies these methods, so ensuring their effective properties and operational properties in EMI evaluation.

articleTitle: Modelling and prediction of EMI coupling through antennas mounted on a cylindrical body
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In particular, military aircraft have radar and communication equipment placed on them for different control actions. A typical airborne early warning system normally has a large number of intentional emitters and receptors. Electromagnetic interference can easily be coupled through various antennas used for these purpose. In this paper an aircraft fuselage is modelled as a cylindrical body and the undesired EMI couplings are mathematically calculated and the results are then presented graphically. An algorithm is developed to predict the fundamental, third harmonic and fifth harmonic interference situations. The diffraction introduced by the curved nature of the cylindrical aircraft is considered. A few remedial measures are also suggested.

articleTitle: Some aspects concerning the international and Russian EMC standardization in the field of radio communication
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: EMC standards in field of radio communication exist at both the national and international level. Due to the rapid integration process in the world economy, a continuous improvement of these standards in agreement with international requirements is necessary, taking sometimes into account some national specificities. The paper presents some similarities and differences between the existing Russian, IEC, CENELEC and ETSI standards and ITU-R recommendations in the field of EMC for radio communication. The aim of the paper is to share the experience of the authors with specialists from other countries who are coordinating national standards with existing or "in development" international documents.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering by shielding object in mobile communication system
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic compatibility is a major problem in mobile communications. We analyse the phenomena of electromagnetic wave scattering by obstacles present in the communication path. Here the scattering model consists of an infinite cylindrical conductor near an infinite conducting plane. This scattering problem involving the conducting plane can be exchanged with that of two elliptic cylinders, using the theory of images. Expansion of fields in terms of Mathieu functions is used to analytically describe the scattered field. To apply the boundary conditions, we have used, in the analysis, the addition theorem of Mathieu functions. We obtained an exact solution for the present problem, and the far fields and the near fields are numerically computed for different parameters.

articleTitle: Reflection method generalization for solution of electromagnetic compatability pulse problems for nonrectangular cavities
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper suggests a generalization of the reflection method (ray approximation) for solution EMC problems connected with an investigation of short-pulse propagation in non-rectangular cavities (convex polyhedrons where the dihedral angles are an integer part of /spl pi/). The developed technique is used to resolve the problem of short front pulse penetration into a right angle equiangular triangle prism with a small aperture.

articleTitle: Reduction of EM radiation from electronic equipment at design stage
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A rationalized approach is introduced for reducing the electromagnetic (EM) radiation from electronic equipment by providing shielding in some section of the PCB. An algorithm is developed and implemented to find the appropriate section where shielding is necessary. A composite CAD package is employed to predict the EM radiation from the PCB with and without shielding. This method of reduction of EM radiation is described and validated experimentally. The results obtained are gratifying.

articleTitle: Plasmon-decay model for origin of electromagnetic wave noises in the earthquakes
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A theory is proposed to explain how the electromagnetic waves are created from a strong earthquake center in the Earth. From the increase of strong stress in rock electrons are excited and emitted, and the bulk plasmons and the surface plasmons can be produced. They propagate to the Earth's surface, where the plasmons transfer into electromagnetic waves. Simple order-estimation shows that electromagnetic waves of frequency range 10 kHz-100 MHz should be observed. We can see that many other observation characters are also interpreted by our plasmon-decay model.

articleTitle: A primary study on near field distribution of hand-held transceivers on the horizontal plane
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper studies the near field distribution of a hand-held transceiver, Kenwood model TR2500. Its near field distribution on the horizontal plane is studied in three cases. One case is where the antenna is normal to the ground without the human model. The other two cases are where the angle included between the antenna and the normal line of ground is 45 degrees with the human model and without it respectively. The paper gives the near field contour plots of the transceiver by numerical calculation and experiments. It shows that the fields in most regions decrease when the transceiver is placed close to the human model.

articleTitle: The suppression technique of electromagnetic interference of motor vehicle
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) from motor vehicles and their effect on broadcast radio and television were studied as early as 1944. Their original effect was significantly reduced by the early 1960s. Today, the use of advanced electronically controlled vehicles are widespread. Most of the vehicular functions are now controlled by microprocessors that send electrical instructions to other devices which operate the engine and transmission as well as the implements the machine was designed to use. Ignition noise and vehicular microprocessor controlled system noise are interfering with mobile communication services and devices such as computers. In China, the study of EMI from vehicles began in the 1970s. Due to the lack of enforcement of the rules and regulation, vehicular electromagnetic emission is now interfering with mobile communication, broadcast radio and other devices. This paper describes vehicular EMI and the suppression technique for automobile EMI.

articleTitle: Interference suppression in cochannel relay television system
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper analyses the demands for isolation, in a cochannel relay television system, and introduces the computational method of isolation. Five measures are presented which extend the isolation in receiving-transmitting level differences and reduce some cochannel interference. The measures are directed to building relay stations to a certain extent.

articleTitle: Practical guide to large system SE (shielding effectiveness) test
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: SE testing is rather straight forward when testing one variable at a time, but the complexity multiplies when several variables are involved as a single entity such as the exterior cover system of a large scale computer. This paper describes the processes and problems associated with preparing and performing SE tests on large systems.

articleTitle: Measurement of near field around hand-held transceiver
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In order to study the distribution of the near field of the hand-held transceiver and whether such a strong electromagnetic field may do harm to the health of the user, an automatic measurement system has been built up and the software has been developed. The near field of the model Kenwood TR-2500 hand-held transceiver has been measured. The test result indicated that the field square exceeded 4000 V/sup 2//m/sup 2/ in a wide space around the transceiver, the limit value of ANSI C95.1-1982 protection guidelines, and it may do harm to the health of the user. It is recommended that the transceiver be held at least 25 cm from the face when transmitting.

articleTitle: Design of antijamming in microwave remote-vision system
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the design of a helix filter used to suppress the jamming in a microwave remote-vision system, analyses the mathematical model of the helix filter and gives the design of the helix filter with a frequency bandwidth from 566 MHz to 578 MHz.

articleTitle: The measurement and analysis of radiated power for program control mini-switchboard
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper briefly presents the electromagnetic radiated emission mechanism of a program control mini-switchboard and the principle method of measurement of radiated emission using a TEM cell. It gives the calculating formulas of the equivalent radiated power of the equipment under test (EUT) in free space. It also gives the emission measurement result of a CLT-8 program control mini-switchboard in the frequency band 0.15 MHz/spl sim/30 MHz and gives further analysis.

articleTitle: EMC design in a microprocessor based system
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the EMI control measures to be taken for the design of printed circuits which use high speed microprocessors. The paper also includes some EMI measurement results of the microprocessor based system.

articleTitle: Educational comments on the wide band transmission characteristics of an inserted different line
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An inserted line which has different mode or characteristic impedance from the 50 /spl Omega/ system shows interesting wide band transmission and reflection characteristics. It suggests a general concept to explain most of the electromagnetic energy transfer concerning EMC phenomena.

articleTitle: Increased surge voltages caused by EMC chokes
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Bi-winding EMC chokes used in telephone equipment increase the peak wire voltages on fast rising surges. Two, choke actions cause this. Choke saturation suddenly releases extra surge energy to the equipment. In the differential mode the chokes transformer action creates larger inter-wire voltages. The paper quantifies this previously unreported affect.

articleTitle: On the effects of bianisotropic covers on PCB radiation
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The effects of a bianisotropic cover on a printed radiating structure are addressed. These effects are studied from the point of view of the field radiated by the printed structure, evaluated in the spectral domain. The numerical results of the radiated emissions due to a microstrip line show the effective advantages of the use of a bianisotropic cover instead of a dielectric one.

articleTitle: EMI caused by a grounding loop
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: EMI caused by a grounding loop is described, investigated and controlled. A new grounding system is designed and it is shown that it is a successful design for EMC.

articleTitle: A study on design of EMI line noise filters
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Line noise filters are used to suppress conductive noise of electrical machinery and apparatus. In general, this filter composition is chosen by a trial and error method. Therefore, in order to carry out a theoretical design of the line noise filters, we studied an equivalent circuit for the line noise filters using the attenuation characteristic of the filters. As a result, we found that we can derive an equivalent circuit for line noise filters which is similar to actual filters, by means of adjusting the parts element of the filter.

articleTitle: Assessing how safe are the rural tin-shed houses in the vicinity of EM fields of the cross-country power lines
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: High voltage grid lines are mostly routed through rural areas. In the countries with high population densities it is difficult to keep the rural houses very far from the lines' routes. For low cost the dwelling houses of the rural people in Bangladesh and a number of Asian countries are usually roofed with thin, galvanized and corrugated steel sheets termed 'tin'. An analysis of the electromagnetic induction effects on a tin-shed house from a nearby power line has not yet been reported in the literature. This paper presents the way this practical issue has been investigated thoroughly. The induced circulating current densities and resulting power dissipation in the roofs of tin-shed houses neighbouring to a 132 kV and a 230 kV transmission line have been quantified as a function of the distance of the nearest edge of a tin sheet from the line, the tin sheet's slant angle with respect to the vertical plane and the height of the roof. The results of this investigation would help the electric utility planners in defending a renewed public concern about transmission lines' effects upon the health of rural mass.

articleTitle: A high-quality ultra-wideband omni-direction antenna
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A wideband omni-direction antenna is designed through using a new biconical model and the method of moments. A frequency band of ten octaves is realized, and the characteristics of the radiation pattern at high frequencies is also improved. A wire grid structure is used to better the physical features of the antenna.

articleTitle: Interference effects for pico-cell indoor personal communication systems
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Personal communication systems (PCS) have recently undergone tremendous growth, enhancing the number of users and the risks of interference. The PCS are extensively used also inside buildings (indoors). This paper presents a thorough analysis and empirical computation of 2nd generation CT-2 digital PCS indoor interference effects, operation ranges and reception quality. The outdoor mutual interference effects analysed previously (Gavan, 1995) are significantly reduced due to shadowing and can be neglected compared to the indoor self interference effects limited mainly by noise floor. The influence of obstructions and floors on fading, shadowing and bit error rate (BER) are considered as well as the advantage of polarization diversity for the system base station antennas.

articleTitle: Effect of chirp on light pulse propagation in dispersive media
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Chirp technology of a light pulse is often used in the light wave transmission to compensate for the pulse distortion due to fiber dispersion; in particular the chirped Bragg fiber grating as a potential dispersion compensator is attractive. In this paper based on the time-space analogy theory, we discuss the effect of chirp on light pulse propagation in detail. This discussion will be helpful for the design of chirped Bragg fiber gratings.

articleTitle: A study on the resistor array network for the optimum termination of a large TEM cell
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the optimum termination method of a TEM cell, in which hybrid termination resistor array networks are utilized. The current stream on the septum, and on the terminal end of a TEM cell is analyzed by numerical analysis. Based on the result of the circuit analysis, the optimum resistor array network is designed, which assures efficient power dissipation, and straight and a uniform current stream. Thermovision photos were taken for comparing the above mentioned network with the conventional termination network on which each resistor is arranged for uniform current distribution. The results of thermovision photos show a good agreement with those obtained by numerical analysis.

articleTitle: Fast channel assignment in irregular radio systems
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method is presented for channel assignment in irregular radio systems, based on the notion of 'spectral blocks'. It combines speed with the potential to produce more spectrally efficient assignments than previously published algorithms. It could also be used for dynamic channel assignment in personal communications networks.

articleTitle: The use of GPS in mobile field strength measurement system
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper puts forward the use of the GPS in a mobile field strength measurement system. The paper analyses the influence of GPS's error in mobile field strength measurement and discusses its achievement and effects.

articleTitle: Effective testing of computerized equipment for EMC immunity to fast electrical transients
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: One of the major problems in testing computerized equipment for immunity to electrical transients is their time-variant susceptibility. Since complete immunity testing of an operational cycle with hundreds of susceptible time windows is prohibitive this paper aims at providing methods for affordable estimation of the mean and maximum malfunction probability in an operational cycle. For the latter reinforcement learning algorithms are used which automatically restrict testing to most susceptible time windows.
