This allows affordable testing also for safety-related equipment and supports effective redesign.

articleTitle: Multimedia in EMC education
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Undergraduate electrical engineer's education in the Marine Technical University includes an EMC course of up to 85 hours. Lectures, 10 laboratory experiments and individual course work are on the schedule. Computer simulation has been used for EMC training for many years. The first step in multimedia software was a slide presentation of EMP testing with sound and explanation. The next step was the development of animation to give information about testing procedures. The last step is interactive multimedia training software compiled video, animation, hypertext, voice and music.

articleTitle: A study of 12 GHz band circularly polarized high-gain radial line slot antenna
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Characteristics of a novel planar antenna which can radiate a circularly polarized pencil beam in the 12 GHz band are presented for the application of receiving direct broadcasts from a satellite. The measured performance of a model antenna with a diameter of 610 mm is presented. Antenna gain of 36 dB and axial ratio of about 1 dB are realized at 12 GHz. The efficiency of this antenna is 70 percent.

articleTitle: Highly sensitive humidity sensor for dielectric measurement (water absorption) in glass-fiber resins
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A humidity sensor using a sensitive capacitive-dependent crystal is described. Presented is the probe sensitivity (dependence of df on the dCx). In addition, the idea of excitation of the entire humidity sensor with stochastic test signals is described and the humidity surface-measuring method is given. It includes the influence of test signals on the weighting function uncertainty and on the A/D-D/A conversion. The results of air-humidity measurement and water absorption measurement in glass-fiber resins are shown experimentally. The uncertainty of the surface humidity measurement is less than 0.2% (T=15-25/spl deg/C and air-humidity=50 to 98%).

articleTitle: Comparing Euro-norms to military standards
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A comparison of commercial Euro-standards and international military standards is made with respect to dual purpose equipment and CE certification under the European EMC directive 89/336/EEC.

articleTitle: Measurement for radiated susceptibility of electronic accurate equipments using a ATEM cell
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a method for measuring the radiated susceptibility of electronic equipment accurately using an asymmetric transverse electromagnetic transmission cell (ATEM cell). The ATEM cell is in closed form with a total length of 2.6 m. The main cross section appears in an asymmetrical square form with dimensions of 1.2 m/spl times/1.2 m. The height of the upper half space is 0.3 m and height of the lower one is 0.9 m. Some wave-absorbing materials, a slideway and a revolving platform are installed in it. Its working frequency covers from DC to 500 MHz, and the standard field strength in it ranges from 10 /spl mu/V/m to 170 V/m. The ATEM cell can be used to test an IBM personal computer or other electronic equipment which are placed in the cell during the test. The measuring process on radiated susceptibility is controlled by a computer. It has many virtues such as a wide working frequency range, no electromagnetic radiated pollution, easy operation and higher accuracy etc.

articleTitle: A hybrid method on calculating EM coupling in large problem spaces
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper establishes a FDTD method combined with the network topology for calculating the EM coupling and transmission. The problem of EM coupling in a large scale space can be divided into simpler questions by cutting the whole problem space into independent sub-regions according to conducting boundaries. The scatter characteristic of every sub-region is calculated independently using the FDTD. A generalized matrix equation expressing the relations among wave vectors in every port is given. The structures of irises in waveguides are taken as numerical examples. This method is useful in analysing complex systems in EMC design and prediction.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic compatibility of broadcast receivers
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper introduces the interference and immunity characteristics of broadcast receivers as well as test methods of harmonic current emissions injected into the power supply interference by broadcast receivers and associated equipment.

articleTitle: The study on electromagnetic noise of satellite ground station
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: During the design of a satellite ground station, a large number of calculation formulas and complicated procedures may be involved, which causes unreasonable performance and price ratio and great waste. The authors of this paper, having comprehensively studied the link formulas and some engineering experiences on satellite receiving, and through strict mathematic deductions, have set up a new mathematic model on the antenna diameter and unweighted video S/N: D=10/sup x/. Where x=0.05S/N-0.05EIRP-10.91598564-0.5Lg/spl eta/+Lgd+0.05/spl Delta/L+0.5Lg(T/sub a/+T/sub r/)-Lg/spl Delta/f/sub v/+1.5Lgf/sub v/-0.05F. D: caliber size (diameter) of the satellite receiving antenna (m). S/N: video signal to noise ratio (dB). EIRP: equivalent wall directional radiation from the satellite to the area where the ground station is (dB/spl middot/w). /spl eta/: antenna efficiency, usually is taken as 0.65 in engineering. d: distance from satellite to ground station (m). /spl Delta/L: down-going additional loss (dB). /spl Delta/fv: video frequency deviation (Hz). fv: Max. video frequency (Hz). F: deacentuation improving factor. Ta: antenna noise temperature. Tr: HF tuner noise temperature. The unweighted video S/N can directly indicate the quality of pictures (which is usually required by users). The establishment of this formula gives a direct relationship between the antenna diameter D and the S/N, and makes it possible to draw a D-S/N curve, showing that the D-S/N relationship is not a linear one. The satellite receiving antenna costs one-third of the total ground station, and the cost of the antenna is proportional to the square of the antenna diameter D. Therefore, the accuracy of antenna diameter is rather critical. The designer may accurately and quickly find out the D value by using the D-S/N curve when designing a specific satellite ground receiving station.

articleTitle: NSA and resonance in a semi-anechoic chamber in low frequency
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: As a result of the continuing growth of high speed electronic systems and equipment in the world, EMI (electromagnetic interference) is becoming a big problem. Specifications for the purpose of imposing maximum acceptable levels of noise that can be radiated from electronic systems and equipment have been published. Almost all the electronic products in the world should be tested to ensure compliance to these specifications. The tests should be performed over a wide frequency range of 30 to 1000 Mhz, either in open field test sites or inside anechoic chambers. For the open field test sites, the tests can be time consuming and expensive at the mercy of the environment, both natural and manmade. Many absorber lined chambers have been established for EMC tests in the world. To simulate an open test site, designers of these chambers must consider controlling reflection within the chamber and shielding the chamber from transmitting or receiving radio wave interference. To ensure whether a chamber is suitable for EMC tests, many regulations have been published such as ANSI C63.4, CISPR 16 and prEN50147-2. The criterion is the deviation from an ideal free-field transmission factor between a source and a receiving antenna, the so-called normalized site attenuation (NSA). The NSA is often measured to confirm whether the chamber satisfies the characteristics required. Problems often come out in the low frequency range. In this paper one reason which may cause the irregularity is discussed.

articleTitle: An improved characteristic based methods for the time-domain Maxwell equations
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An improved characteristic-based numerical algorithm is presented for solving the time-dependent Maxwell equations. A new term of the matrix is added to the original equations which are rewritten in vector form on a Cartesian frame to fully describe the features of the complex spatial conditions. The implicit scheme is also drawn into the formulation to separate the six field vectors. In order to better depict wave motion the three forward and backward differential methods are used according to the eigenvalues of the coefficient matrices.

articleTitle: Case study: prediction of RFI effects of electrified railways on aeronautical radio navigation stations
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The case is that an electrified railway line is 300 meters away across an airport runway. The paper studies both of active and passive radio frequency interference caused by the electrified railways to aeronautical radio navigation stations, especially to instrument landing systems (ILS). The EMC prediction model has been built. The prediction results agreed with the results of the actual flying check test.

articleTitle: The current status of the IEC 1000-4-X Basic EMC Standards
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To many manufacturers, the IEC 1000-4-X series of Basic EMC Standards seems to be constantly changing. Manufacturers are concerned about pending changes to test standards which may require the purchase of new simulators, modifications of test facilities, or re-writing test plans and procedures. This paper outlines the operation of the task forces and working groups responsible for developing new 1000-4-X series standards, and brings the reader up-to-date on pending new documents, revisions or changes, and proposed amendments to existing standards.

articleTitle: The study of higher frequency seismogenic EM emissions based on the observation results of "Kobe earthquake"
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: For the Kobe earthquake, many higher frequency seismogenic EM emissions were observed in the MF, HF and VHF bands. From our investigation, the exciting energy is transferred by impulsive magnetic fields from the focus to the epicenter area. The excited higher frequency electromagnetic waves at a highly conductive slot consisted of a slit antenna along the fault zone.

articleTitle: Power frequency interference rejection in power line carrier communication
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A simple adaptive notch filter with infinite impulse response (IIR) is developed for eliminating power frequency interference in power line carrier communication. The adaptive IIR notch filter has a minimal number of adjustable coefficients and can be realized easily in real-time processing. The performance function of the notch filter is unimodal for a single interference frequency from a broad-band signal, and gradient-based algorithms are used. For several interference frequencies the cascade with the single structure is realized two or more times. Experimental results demonstrate its performance.

articleTitle: The affection on CDMA system caused by electromagnetic environment of 800 MHz cellular frequency
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: External interference is discussed in the paper and the discussion focuses on the effect on a CDMA system. The cost of external interference can be assessed by translating its impact into an equivalent rise in cell site noise figure. This increase results in a decreased cell coverage. This effect indicates that a -108 dBm interference results in a 30% reduction in coverage area at any loading.

articleTitle: Optical signal processing of interference and fading effects in high bit rate mobile communication
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: High bit rate and high speed mobile radio communications using microwaves and millimeter waves are very attractive for wireless mega and giga bits LAN and video transmissions. Radio interferences due to multi-propagation paths and multiple scattering by street buildings and natural structures of hills and trees are very important problems for high bit rate mobile radio communications. Real time high speed signal processing for delayed fading noises may be required. Optical signal processing using optical and radio interactions are most useful to accomplish real time high speed signal processing. Fundamental properties and applications of optical signal processors using optical active waveguide devices are shown for high bit-rate mobile communications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic scattering from multiple slots in thick conducting screen terminated by a common load
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper considers a type of problem in which there are multiple slots in a thick conducting screen, and they are terminated with a common microwave network. The theoretical results are given.

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of electromagnetic radiation of city rapid guided transit systems
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The measurement results of electromagnetic radiation (ER) emitted from Beijing metro system were introduced. The measurement were carried out under varied circumstances such as different locations, different locomotive working conditions and different power facilities. The distribution characteristics of the ER in the frequency domain under the above circumstances and the distribution law of the ER along the line were derived. Useful conclusions have been work out by analysis.

articleTitle: Dipole-image model for origin of electromagnetic wave noises in the earthquakes
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A theory is proposed to explain how electromagnetic waves are created from a strong earthquake center in the Earth. From an increase of the high stress in rock exo-electrons are excited, and there appears an instant dipole, from which the image of the dipole appears inside the Earth. Then we can observe electromagnetic waves emitted by the dipole-image appearance and change. We show that many observation characters of the electromagnetic waves are explained by our dipole-image model.

articleTitle: Lightning protection in Chinese railway traffic control system
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The article provides information obtained from an investigation of the statistics of damage caused by lightning strikes. Several typical examples of Chinese railway system, which was damaged by lightning strikes are included, the mechanisms are analysed, and the protection measures are examined.

articleTitle: Interference and elimination techniques in the infrared remote control system (IRCS)
publicationTitle: 1997 Proceedings of International Symposium on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper begins with an analysis on all disturbing sources in an IRCS (infrared remote control system), and introduces corresponding approaches, such as photoelectric coupling, reasonable grounding, signal modulation, digital filter, detection, etc. applied in the hardware and the software to suppress interference, widen the control distance and improve the control accuracy. By doing these, the paper provides a preparation for further research on applying this system in suitable situations.
